balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
Daiwa House reports seven operating segments: Single-Family Houses and Condominiums (new-build sales, cyclical and tied to Japan's housing-starts volume), Rental Housing and Existing Homes (brokerage/remodeling, more recurring), Commercial Facilities and Logistics/Business & Corporate Facilities (development and leasing to corporate tenants), and Environment & Energy (renewables, broken out from FY2022).

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: group revenue has grown every year even as HousesSold (the Single-Family Houses volume driver) fell FY2021-FY2025 -- the mix is shifting from one-off house sales toward Rental Housing, Commercial Facilities and Logistics, which carry more recurring income. Existing Homes was folded into Other from FY2023, so that line's apparent drop is a reclassification, not a business change.

What to watch:

  • Whether Rental Housing + Commercial + Logistics keep growing faster than Single-Family Houses
  • Environment & Energy's small but growing share
  • Reclassifications between segments distorting year-over-year comparisons

segmentOperatingProfit.title: Operating profit by segment
segmentOperatingProfit.content:
The same seven segments as the revenue chart, but at the operating-profit line -- shows which businesses actually earn the margin, not just the sales.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: compare each segment's profit share here against its revenue share on the chart above -- Rental Housing and Commercial Facilities have historically carried fatter margins than new-house construction, so a segment can matter more to earnings than its revenue share suggests.

What to watch:

  • Segments growing revenue but not profit (margin compression)
  • How much of group operating profit now comes from recurring leasing/management versus one-off construction sales

housingVolume.title: Houses sold and Japan housing starts
housingVolume.content:
Houses sold is Daiwa House's own annual unit volume in the Single-Family Houses segment; Japan housing starts is the whole-market total (thousands of units) the company sells into.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: HousesSold has fallen every year since FY2017 (54,925 to 32,239 in FY2025), roughly tracking the broader Japan starts decline -- this is the external volume headwind that makes the shift toward Rental Housing, Commercial Facilities and Logistics revenue (see the segment-mix charts) the central diversification story.

What to watch:

  • Daiwa House's unit volume falling faster or slower than the national starts figure (share gain/loss)
  • Whether rising average house prices are offsetting falling unit volume in segment revenue

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Daiwa House Industry Co., Ltd.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
